title: United Express 6291
summary: A BAe Jetstream 41 on approach to Columbus in weather with cloud overcast 800 feet, visibility 2.5 miles in light snow and fog, descended through 1,250 feet when stick shaker activated twice for 3 seconds each. The aircraft continued descending below the glide slope in a high nose-up attitude and collided with trees 1.2 miles short of the runway. Both pilots lacked experience with electronic flight instrument systems and failed to perform proper stall recovery. The investigation found the crew maintained an unstable approach, failed to maintain airspeed and altitude, and improperly responded to the stall warning.
probable_cause: The crew conducted a poorly planned and unstable approach, failed to maintain both airspeed and altitude during descent, and improperly responded to the stall warning. The inexperienced first officer and captain with history of failed check rides compounded the situation. The airline failed to provide adequate training and stabilized approach criteria.

events.text: Flight 6291 departed from Dulles at 9:58 p.m. EST for 90-minute flight to Columbus
Columbus approach control contacted; captain advised descending through 13,200 feet to 11,000 feet. Controller assigned 285-degree heading to intercept ILS runway 28L and cleared to 10,000 feet
Updated weather reported cloud overcast 800 feet, visibility 2.5 miles in light snow and fog, wind 300 degrees at 4 knots
Runway 28L ILS approach clearance issued; clearance to land on runway 28L granted two minutes later
Aircraft descending through 1,250 feet, stick shaker activated and sounded for 3 seconds
Captain asked in alarmed manner Tony! What did you do?
After 1.5 seconds, stick shaker sounded again
Aircraft collided with stand of trees in high nose-up attitude, 1.2 miles short of runway
